target.title: Add item search endpoint
target.description:
The storefront needs a simple way to search the catalogue by name.
Adds GET /items/search?q=<term>, available to any logged-in user.

summary: Adds a new GET /items/search endpoint that allows logged-in users to search for items by name.

suspects.title: SQL Injection vulnerability in item search query
suspects.problem: The search query uses Python f-strings to concatenate the raw term variable directly into the SQL statement, which allows SQL injection if an attacker supplies malicious input in the 'q' parameter.
suspects.how_to_check: Check how db.query is implemented across the repository to see if it accepts parameterized queries (e.g., passing parameters as a tuple/dict) rather than raw formatted strings.

text:
Investigate this suspected problem.

Suspect S1: SQL Injection vulnerability in item search query
Category: security
Location: app/routes/items.py lines 33-35 (new version)
Suspected problem: The search query uses Python f-strings to concatenate the raw term variable directly into the SQL statement, which allows SQL injection if an attacker supplies malicious input in the 'q' parameter.
What would confirm or refute it: Check how db.query is implemented across the repository to see if it accepts parameterized queries (e.g., passing parameters as a tuple/dict) rather than raw formatted strings.

The planner's summary of the pull request: Adds a new GET /items/search endpoint that allows logged-in users to search for items by name.

Budget: 6 turns (each reply is one turn), up to 3 tool calls per turn. Finish with submit_verdict.

arguments.explanation: In app/routes/items.py, the newly added search_items function uses Python f-strings to concatenate the raw term variable directly into the SQL SELECT statement (SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%' ORDER BY name LIMIT 50). Since db.query accepts parameterized queries (sql, params), using f-string interpolation instead of query parameters allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL commands via the 'q' query parameter.
arguments.claim: The search endpoint in items.py uses an f-string to concatenate user input directly into the SQL statement, causing an SQL injection vulnerability.
arguments.suggested_fix: Change the query to use query parameters: db.query("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name LIKE ? ORDER BY name LIMIT 50", (f"%{term}%",))

evidence.note: The search_items endpoint uses an f-string with unescaped term variable directly inside the SQL query string passed to db.query
Database.query supports parameterized queries via the params tuple argument
Other endpoints use parameterized queries properly with db.query
